**Microsoft Learn – “Create and delete pods” (Azure AKS)**  
This Microsoft Learn article explains what a Kubernetes Pod is, why it’s the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes, and how it runs a single application instance on a node. It also walks through the lifecycle of a pod and shows how to create and delete a pod with `kubectl` commands, plus a sample YAML definition.  

*Key points*  
| Topic | Summary | Source |
|-------|---------|--------|
| Definition | A pod is a single instance of an app that can contain one or more containers sharing the same host, IP, and storage. | [Create and delete pods](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks-hybrid-edge/windows-server/create-pods) |
| Lifecycle | Pods are scheduled to run on nodes, live until the containers inside them finish or are removed, and are managed via standard Kubernetes APIs. | Same page |
| CLI usage | `kubectl run … --restart=Never` creates a single pod; `kubectl get pods`, `kubectl describe pod <name>`, and `kubectl delete pod <name>` manage it. | Same page |
| YAML example | Shows a minimal pod manifest (`apiVersion`, `kind: Pod`, `metadata`, `spec` with a container). | Same page |

---
